subject: chemistry
examFormat: Chemistry is one of the three sections in the single combined EJU Science (理科) booklet; examinees choose 2 of the 3 subjects and answer on a mark-sheet (one subject per side). The 2 chosen subjects share an 80-minute limit. The chemistry section spans roughly pages 23-37 (sometimes to 40) of the booklet and consists of a flat list of 20 independent numbered questions (問1-問20, answer rows 1-20). There are no Roman-numeral super-blocks like physics; questions simply progress roughly in syllabus order: structure of matter and bonding first, then states/equilibria/stoichiometry, then inorganic chemistry, then organic and polymers. Every item is single-best-answer multiple choice (choose ONE from typically 5-8 options). Answer formats include: pick the false/correct statement among 5; pick the matching combination from a table (e.g. choose the row giving the right (a),(b),(c) assignment); 'two of the following are correct/wrong, choose the pair'; numeric calculation choosing the closest value; and choosing a structural formula or crystal-classification. A periodic table (group/period grid with only H labeled) and a standard constants block are printed at the start of the section. Text is Japanese with extensive bilingual glossing of chemical terms (English in parentheses). No calculator; numeric answers are designed for hand calculation and you select the closest listed value.

constants.atomicWeightsNote: A short atomic-weight list is given per paper and varies by paper (e.g. H 1.0, C 12, O 16; plus a few elements the paper actually needs such as Na, Al, Cl, Ca, Cu, Mg, Br).

keywords: ポリエチレンテレフタラート

questionArchetypes.description: Counting particles / electron configuration: a table or list of statements about numbers of protons/neutrons/electrons, shell occupancy, or valence electrons for given atoms/ions; choose the one statement (or value) that is wrong, or choose the same-group pair from electron configurations.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Five statements give a quantity (column A) and its claimed value (column B), e.g. 'electrons in H+ = 0', 'neutrons in Cl = 20'; choose the row whose B value is wrong. (2021_1 Q1; same-group-from-config variant 2018_2 Q1)

questionArchetypes.description: Bonding / electron pairs / molecular shape: among several molecules/ions choose the one with the most shared (or unshared) electron pairs, or the one that is NOT planar, or classify the crystal type (ionic/covalent/molecular) of given solids via a table.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Among NH3, N2, H2S, oxonium ion, ammonium ion, choose the species with the most shared electron pairs. (2021_1 Q2; non-planar-molecule variant 2021_1 Q3; crystal-classification table 2021_1 Q4; double-bond+lone-pair 2019_1 Q3)

questionArchetypes.description: Stoichiometry / limiting reactant calculation: a reaction with given amounts (often from a data table of mass vs gas volume) where one reactant runs out; compute a maximum reacting mass and/or the concentration of the other reagent, or the mass/number of atoms of product, choosing the closest value.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Various masses of Mg react with 4.0 mL HCl; H2 volumes are tabulated and plateau. Find the maximum mass of Mg that reacts and the HCl concentration. (2021_1 Q5; metal-carbonate molar-mass variant 2020_2 Q3; CaCO3+HCl excess variant 2019_1 Q5)

questionArchetypes.description: Gas / vapor-pressure calculation: a closed variable-volume container with a reaction or a gas mixture; using ideal-gas law, partial pressures, and a given vapor pressure, find the volume at which all water vaporizes, or a partial pressure, choosing the closest value.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: H2 (1.0e-3 mol) and O2 (5.0e-3 mol) ignite, water forms; at 33C the volume is increased until all water becomes vapor (vapor pressure 5.0e3 Pa). Find that volume. (2021_1 Q6)

questionArchetypes.description: Colligative / solubility calculation: recrystallization with solubility values, or ranking freezing points of solutions by effective particle concentration (electrolyte dissociation), choosing the order or the precipitated mass.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: 200 g of saturated KNO3 at 60C is evaporated (20 g water) then cooled to 20C; using solubilities 109 (60C) and 32 (20C), find the mass of KNO3 that crystallizes. (2019_1 Q8; freezing-order of urea/NaCl/CaCl2 solutions 2018_2 Q7)

questionArchetypes.description: Unit-cell / density calculation: given a unit cell (bcc/fcc or NaCl-type) with edge length and atomic weight, derive the density expression g/cm^3 or compute its numeric value using N_A.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A bcc unit cell of potassium has edge a; express the density in terms of M, a, N_A. (2020_2 Q5; NaCl density numeric value 2018_2 Q10)

questionArchetypes.description: Thermochemistry calculation: combustion/formation heat used to warm water (Q = m c dT), find the heat of formation/combustion in kJ/mol; or qualitative statements about a thermochemical equilibrium (effect of T, catalyst, pressure on amounts/equilibrium constant).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Burning 4.2 g H2 warms 15 kg water by 10C; with c=4.2 J/(g.K) find the heat of formation of water in kJ/mol. (2020_2 Q6; methane-combustion temperature-rise variant 2019_1 Q6; HI equilibrium qualitative 2021_1 Q10)

questionArchetypes.description: Redox identification or titration: identify which underlined species acts as oxidizing/reducing agent in given equations, or which gases released show reducing action; or a redox-titration volume calculation (e.g. KMnO4 needed to oxidize H2O2).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Among five equations choose the one where the underlined species acts as the oxidizing agent. (2020_2 Q9). Also: volume of 0.200 mol/L KMnO4 needed to fully oxidize 50.0 mL of 0.300 mol/L H2O2 in acid. (2021_1 Q8)

questionArchetypes.description: Electrolysis / Faraday calculation or cell labeling: given a current and time (or total gas volume), find charge in C, or the substance and mass deposited at an electrode; or identify the species oxidized/reduced and product in a fuel cell.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Dilute H2SO4 is electrolyzed with Pt electrodes; 672 mL of gas total at STP. Find the charge passed in C. (2021_1 Q9; molten NaCl cathode product/mass 2020_2 Q10; multi-cell series 2018_2 Q9; fuel-cell A/B/C labeling 2019_1 Q10)

questionArchetypes.description: Acid-base reasoning: compare ion concentrations / titration amounts for strong vs weak acids at equal pH; identify a salt fitting given properties (e.g. from a divalent acid and monovalent base, pH>7); or judge true/false pH statements; or recognize water acting as an acid/base.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Find the salt that is both (a) from a divalent acid and monovalent base and (b) has pH>7. (2021_1 Q7; strong-vs-weak-acid concentration comparison 2020_2 Q8; water-as-acid identification 2021_1 Q13; Bronsted base identification 2018_2 Q6)

questionArchetypes.description: Properties of main-group elements: true/false statements about a group (e.g. group 2 flame colors, solubility of hydroxides/sulfates; halogen acidity/reactivity; properties of phosphorus, sulfur dioxide); choose the correct/incorrect statement or the property common to all listed elements.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Among five statements about group-2 elements (flame color, reaction with cold water, hydroxide/chloride/sulfate solubility) choose the correct one. (2020_2 Q11; SO2 false-statement 2021_1 Q14; halogen errors-pair 2020_2 Q12; phosphorus 2019_1 Q12)

questionArchetypes.description: Metal-ion separation / qualitative analysis: a solution of one or more metal ions shows precipitation behavior with NaOH/NH3/HCl/NaCl/H2S; identify the metal ion present, or which ions remain in the filtrate after sequential reagent additions, or which solution gives no precipitate with a reagent.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A colorless solution: NaOH gives a precipitate that redissolves in excess; NH3 gives a precipitate that redissolves in excess; NaCl gives no precipitate. Identify the metal ion (Ag+/Ca2+/Mg2+/Pb2+/Zn2+/Al3+). (2021_1 Q15; Al3+/Fe3+/Zn2+ filtrate-after-NH3-then-NaOH 2018_2 Q15; no-precipitate-set 2019_1 Q13; Ag+ vs Pb2+ 2020_2 Q15)

questionArchetypes.description: Transition-metal chemistry or reactivity series: true/false about copper/iron/silver/zinc compounds and reactions; or which metal fits a set of dissolution clues (which dissolve in dilute acid, passivation in conc. HNO3, displacement); or which displacement reaction does not proceed by ionization tendency.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Statements (a)-(e) about Ag/Cu/Fe/Zn (dissolving in dil. H2SO4, displacement, passivation in conc. HNO3); choose the A-D metal assignment. (2019_1 Q15; copper-compound true/false 2020_2 Q14; non-proceeding displacement 2018_2 Q14; gas reducing-action 2020_2 Q13)

questionArchetypes.description: Hydrocarbon isomers / addition reasoning: count isomers of a formula meeting a structural condition (e.g. having a C=C double bond, or giving an asymmetric carbon on Br2 addition); or compute the molecular weight of a bromine-addition product of a cyclic unsaturated hydrocarbon; or true/false on ethylene/acetylene reactions.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: For C3H5Br, count isomers with one C=C double bond, and how many give an asymmetric carbon on Br2 addition. (2021_1 Q16; molecular weight of cyclic bromide product 2021_1 Q19; ethylene true/false 2021_1 Q17)

questionArchetypes.description: Functional-group reactions / identification: identify products of named small-molecule reactions (e.g. dry distillation, CaC2 + water, oxidation of alcohols); or deduce an alcohol structure from silver-mirror + iodoform clues; or which single compound among several undergoes a given test (NaHCO3, Na, silver mirror, iodoform).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: An ester C5H10O2 hydrolyzes to a carboxylic acid (gives silver mirror) and an alcohol (gives iodoform); choose the alcohol's structural formula. (2020_2 Q16; products of CH3COONa/NaOH, (CH3COO)2Ca dry-distillation, CaC2+H2O 2020_2 Q17; single-compound reaction 2018_2 Q17; ethanol/acetic-acid true/false 2019_1 Q16,Q17)

questionArchetypes.description: Aromatic separation / properties: separate nitrobenzene/benzoic acid/aniline among ether, dilute HCl, and NaOH layers (choose the table row); or count C7H8O isomers and how many give FeCl3 coloration; or true/false about substituted-benzene structures.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: An ether solution of nitrobenzene, benzoic acid, and aniline is extracted with dilute HCl then NaOH; choose which compound ends up in each layer. (2020_2 Q18; C7H8O isomer counts and FeCl3 coloration 2018_2 Q18; structure true/false 2019_1 Q19)

questionArchetypes.description: Polymers / natural macromolecules: identify which polymers use formaldehyde in synthesis, or which contains nitrogen, or match polymer to polymerization type and constituent elements; or true/false about proteins, or shared properties of starch and cellulose.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Among phenol resin, PET, polystyrene, vinylon, poly(vinyl chloride), choose the pair that uses formaldehyde in synthesis. (2021_1 Q20; nitrogen-free polymer 2019_1 Q20; polymer/type/element match 2020_2 Q19; protein true/false 2020_2 Q20; starch-vs-cellulose 2018_2 Q20)

styleNotes: Generate exactly 20 independent single-best-answer items (問1-問20) in roughly syllabus order: ~Q1-5 structure/bonding/mole, ~Q6-10 states/equilibrium/thermochem/redox/electrolysis, ~Q11-15 inorganic (typical elements, transition metals, ion separation), ~Q16-20 organic and polymers. Mix calculation items ('choose the closest value', usually 5-6 numeric options) with qualitative items ('choose the correct/incorrect statement', 'two are correct - choose the pair', or a combination-table where you pick the row that correctly assigns a/b/c). Use the printed constants exactly (STP molar volume 22.4 L/mol, R=8.31x10^3 Pa.L/(K.mol), N_A=6.02x10^23, F=9.65x10^4 C/mol) and provide only the atomic weights the item needs. Keep calculations hand-doable with clean numbers; numeric answers select the nearest listed value. Favor authentic devices: data tables (mass vs gas volume), reaction equations with underlined species, separation/precipitation schemes, and 'structural formula' or 'crystal type' choices. Gloss chemical terms bilingually (Japanese with English in parentheses) as the real exam does. Cover the full breadth - do not over-weight calculations; about half of recent items are conceptual/qualitative. One concept per item; difficulty matches Japanese high-school 'Advanced Chemistry' (standard university-entrance level).
